LESSON: FOODS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Our Family
Topic 2.1: Foods
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Foods, part of Our Family in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we eat food? 2. How do you choose the types of food you eat?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Foods together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Citizenship: learner develops active community life skills when naming different types of food eaten by family members.

Values:
● Unity: learner collaboratively match pictures of fruits eaten by family members.

• Respect: learner enhances etiquette when talking about ‘do’s’ and ‘don'ts’ while eating.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
• Preventive health: learner enhances eating healthy balanced diet when identifying different types of foods eaten by family

members.

• Learner support programme: learner appreciates cultural diversity when singing songs on different types of foods eaten by

family members.

Link to other learning area:

Foods relates to concepts of creation in Religious Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

Pictures of different foods for healthy body, slant boards, ddifferent types of food eaten by family members, adhesive such as

masking tape, positioning/ seating devices whose worktops/ table tops are at a suitable height, adapted digital devices, head/

mouth pointers, theme-based multi-purpose communication board/ chart with legible print and clear colour contrast, songs and

poems on the importance of eating food,

Other Related Service providers: Physiotherapist, Learner Support Assistant
